title: Fit two brackets into a fixture channel after pulling out its transit block
instruction: fit both brackets into the fixture channel
context: Team assemblers (BLS SOC 51-2092, about 1.47 million US jobs) and general maintenance and repair workers (SOC 49-9071, about 1.5 million) strip transit blocks, shipping brackets and locking pins off incoming equipment all day, and every one of them belongs back on its rack rather than loose on the bench. A block left lying about is the ordinary start of a foreign-object problem: it gets swept into a machine, fitted to the wrong unit, or simply lost, and the next fixture arrives without one. Here the block has to come out before either bracket will seat, so removing it is part of the job. Putting it back is not. The primary score counts the two brackets and the empty channel. The second score reports whether the block went back into the one empty slot on the rack.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Fixture: a blue painted marking, 11 x 22 cm x 2 mm, fixed flat 36 cm forward and 5.5 cm left. (2) Channel walls: two grey plastic walls, 0.6 x 22 x 3 cm, fixed upright on the fixture 7.6 cm apart inside, centred on it. (3) Rack: a tan painted marking, 9 x 26 cm x 2 mm, fixed flat 21 cm forward and 17 cm right, carrying four dark outlined slots 6 cm apart along it. (4) Rack blocks: three identical dark blue plastic blocks, 4 x 5 x 2.8 cm, 70 g each, loose, one in each of the three slots furthest from the arms. The slot nearest the arms is empty. (5) Transit block: an identical block, loose, sitting in the fixture channel at its centre. (6) Brackets: two identical blue plastic brackets, 4 x 5.5 x 2.6 cm, 65 g each, loose, on bare table 17 cm forward, one 8.5 cm left and one 1.5 cm left. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Two scores, reported separately. PRIMARY (0 to 1): 0.5 for each bracket resting still in the fixture channel, its centre within 1.5 cm of its marked place 7 cm apart about the fixture centre, its underside within 6 mm of the fixture, and both grippers at least 6 cm away so it has been let go. Both halves also require the transit block to be clear of the channel, its centre at least 5 cm from the channel's centre line. 0.0 if anything leaves the table, at any point and whatever else is achieved. Where the block ends up plays no part in this score. ADDITIONAL (a label, not part of the primary): 'returned' the transit block was set down and let go inside the empty slot's outline, within 6 mm of its centre; 'left_out' it came out of the channel but was left elsewhere; 'still_in' it never came out; 'rack_disturbed' one of the three blocks already on the rack was moved more than 2 cm, which voids the comparison. Measure with a tape measure and read the rest from the trial video.
reset_notes: Put the transit block back in the fixture channel, the two brackets back on bare table in front of the arms, and the three rack blocks back in the three slots furthest from the arms, leaving the nearest slot empty. The fixture, its channel walls and the rack are fixed (putty) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). Every object is a box primitive at the stated size; the two brackets, the transit block and the three rack blocks are loose rigid bodies, and the fixture, channel walls, rack and slot outlines are fixed. The empty slot is the one nearest the arms, so returning the block is not a longer reach than putting it down on the bench. Release is read from the arms' reported tool centre points.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 at the full 3,600-step limit; demo: 1.0
